chunks: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Book, [that they would] make it clear to mankind and not conceal it, but they cast it away behind their backs and purchased with it a little gain; so wretched was that for which they sold themselves.

key_terms.أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ: Those given the Book (People of the Book)
key_terms.لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ: You will make it clear/expound it

ai.seo_question: What covenant did God take from the People of the Book regarding their scriptures?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific covenant taken from the prophets of the Children of Israel to recognize and proclaim the advent of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Ahl al-Bayt. The phrase 'casting it behind their backs' signifies a deliberate rejection of divine truth in favor of political power and material wealth, a theme frequently cited to illustrate the spiritual decline of the elite classes. This narrative serves as a cautionary example for the Ummah regarding the preservation and authentic transmission of religious knowledge.
